EXP-A1.title: PhysioNet 2016 binary baseline
EXP-A1.notes: Every model runs on the IDENTICAL 25 folds so EXP-A2 pairs with it fold-for-fold. Per-fold values are persisted for the paired tests in Phase 81 - aggregating them away would destroy the statistics chapter.

EXP-A2.title: PhysioNet 2016 binary optimized
EXP-A2.notes: Nested CV. The outer fold is never seen by any search. Selection follows the sensitivity-and-balanced-accuracy rule, not accuracy.

EXP-B1.title: PASCAL set_a four-class
EXP-B1.notes: `artifact` is a RECORDING-QUALITY label, not a cardiac class. This is not a four-class cardiac classifier and must never be described as one (T66.6). Subject IDs are unavailable, so results are record-level only.

EXP-B2.title: PASCAL set_b three-class
EXP-B2.notes: Severe imbalance (320/95/46). Report per-class recall, not accuracy. The report must state explicitly that sets A and B were never merged.

EXP-C2.title: CirCor clinical outcome
EXP-C2.notes: Near-balanced (486/456), unlike every other task here. The patient-level label is propagated to that patient's recordings; the noise this introduces is documented rather than ignored.

EXP-D1.title: Cross-dataset transfer: PhysioNet binary -> CirCor outcome
EXP-D1.population_note: This is ADULT-TO-PAEDIATRIC TRANSFER, not a like-for-like test. PhysioNet has a median age of 25 with 0.3% under 18 and is dominated by adult degenerative disease (CAD 287, MVP 134). CirCor is ~98% paediatric (Child 598, Infant 191, Adolescent 66, Neonate 6). A large performance drop is the EXPECTED consequence of that population mismatch and is NOT evidence that PV-MEPCG fails to generalize. Describe it as "cross-dataset transfer from an adult cohort to a predominantly paediatric cohort" - never as "cross-dataset generalization" unqualified. A write-up claiming otherwise is wrong.

EXP-G1.title: PhysioNet diagnosis multiclass (supplementary, Objective 6)
EXP-G1.notes: Carries Objective 6 properly. PASCAL A cannot: it is 124 records with 19 in one class. Presented as supplementary evidence on a far larger sample, with the small-sample limitation stated and CIs on every per-class metric.
